week1: A country (planned). A country-year panel for the data join.
week2: One row per country: the 2022 cross-section, or one 1990-to-2022 pair.
week3: One row per country and window start year. Windows overlap, so a country appears many times.
why_it_differs: Each week answers a different question.
how_this_report_handles_it: Each result is described with its unit. Counts of countries and counts of windows are never mixed.

week1: A four-way class from growth rates over 1990-2022 (planned).
week2: Absolute decoupling between two end years: CO2 per person lower in 2022 than in 1990 and GDP per person higher.
week3: Absolute decoupling over a rolling three-year window: CO2 per person lower and GDP per person higher after 3 years.
why_it_differs: A 33-year comparison and a 3-year window ask different questions.
how_this_report_handles_it: 'Decoupling' always means absolute decoupling. The word 'long-run' is used for the two-end-year version and 'window' for the three-year version.

week2: 64% of high-income countries and 32% of all countries compared decoupled between 1990 and 2022.
week3: 26.8% of pool windows and 24.9% of test windows were decoupling windows (43% for high income in the test years).
why_it_differs: One counts countries over 33 years; the other counts country windows over three years, and a window can fail simply because of a bad year.
how_this_report_handles_it: Both are shown with their definitions. They are not to be compared directly.

week1: 197 countries in the preliminary 2022 correlation; 6,798 joined country-years in 1990-2022.
week2: 198 countries for H1, 205 for H2, 146 for H3, 74 for H5 and 184 for H6.
week3: 201 countries in the pool and 198 in the test set; 4,687 windows.
why_it_differs: Each analysis needs different variables to be present, so different countries drop out.
how_this_report_handles_it: Every figure and table states its own n.

week1: Current World Bank groups: 76 high, 58 upper-middle, 47 lower-middle and 25 low income in the joined set.
week2: The same current groups, applied to countries with CO2 data in 2022: 74, 59, 47 and 25.
week3: The same current groups, used only to describe results and never as a model feature.
why_it_differs: The counts differ because the samples differ, not because the classification differs.
how_this_report_handles_it: One classification (the current one) throughout, with the caveat that countries have moved between groups.

week1: World Bank GDP per person, constant 2015 US$ (primary); PPP as a check.
week2: The same, with PPP as a robustness variant.
how_this_report_handles_it: Constant 2015 US$ everywhere, unless a PPP check is mentioned.

week1: OWID CO2 per person from fossil fuels and industry, production-based. Consumption-based CO2 planned for 120 countries.
why_it_differs: Consumption-based data were planned but never used.
how_this_report_handles_it: Production-based throughout. The limitation is stated wherever decoupling is mentioned.

week3: Window start years 1993 to 2019 (three-year windows ending 2022 at the latest), look-back from 1988; pool 1993 to 2013, test 2017 to 2019.
why_it_differs: Time-aware validation needs years of history before each window.
how_this_report_handles_it: The over-time figure shows start years 1993 to 2019 and marks the test years.

why_it_differs: One more country is included in Week 2; the preliminary figure was never meant to be final.
how_this_report_handles_it: Week 2's figure is the result. Week 1's is a consistency check.
